q: What are the basic components of a political party?
a: A leader, active members and followers (supporters).

q: Name the three major types of party system.
a: Single-party system, bi-party (two-party) system and multi-party system.

q: Name the countries which follow a bi-party system.
a: The USA (Democratic and Republican parties) and the UK (Labour and Conservative parties).

q: Write a note on coalition government.
a: When no single party wins a majority, two or more parties join together to form the government on an agreed common programme. This is a coalition government. It is common in multi-party systems such as India.

q: Write any four functions of a political party.
a:
1. Contest elections and field candidates.
2. Put forward policies and programmes in their manifestos.
3. Form and run the government if they win a majority.
4. Act as the opposition, criticising and checking the government.
5. Shape public opinion and take people's problems to the government.
6. Play a role in making laws.

q: When is a political party recognised as a National Party?
a:
A party is recognised as a national party if it satisfies any one of these:
1. It wins 6% of valid votes in Lok Sabha or Assembly elections in four or more states and also wins 4 Lok Sabha seats; or
2. It wins at least 2% of Lok Sabha seats (11 seats) from at least three states; or
3. It is recognised as a state party in four or more states.

q: Is a political party necessary for a democratic country?
a: Yes. Parties organise people around ideas, put forward candidates and programmes, form governments and act as the opposition. Without them representatives would be independent individuals, making stable government and accountability difficult. They link people and government and educate voters.

q: Give three names each of national parties, regional parties and registered but unrecognised parties.
a: National parties: Bharatiya Janata Party, Indian National Congress, Communist Party of India (Marxist) (also BSP, AAP, NPP). Regional parties: DMK, AIADMK, Telugu Desam Party, Shiv Sena, Trinamool Congress. Registered but unrecognised parties: many small parties registered with the Election Commission that do not meet the recognition criteria (lists change after each election).
